extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets, creative writers, and readers of literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for poets about the temperament, methods, and aims of poetic creation—how imagination, symbol, renunciation, and engagement with present life produce enduring poetry. Emphasizes the poet's inner passion, use of metamorphosis/tropes, and practical relation to society and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative metamorphosis / use of tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: The imagination effects a metamorphosis that excites in the beholder an emotion of joy; the use of symbols, tropes, fables, oracles and all poetic forms has a power of emancipation and exhilaration for all men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ metamorphosis to reveal 'another world' within this world; examples include Aristotle's and Plato's figurative definitions, Vitruvius relating anatomy to architecture, Orpheus, Proclus, Chaucer, John in Revelation, and Aesop's masquerade of beasts. The imaginative transformation 'touches us by a wand' and liberates readers by giving a new sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value the transcendental and extraordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in books is of value except the transcendental and extraordinary; such departures from routine signal originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questionable or fantastical elements (e.g., angels, magic, astrology in writers like Pythagoras, Swedenborg, Cardan) can be valuable as certificates of departure from routine and witnesses of new thought. Prize work that shows bold, extraordinary vision over mere conventional learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be inflamed by your thought—authentic passion over polish
rubrics_metrics.description: If the imagination intoxicates the poet, if a man is inflamed and carried away by his thought to the degree that he forgets authors and the public, that single dream is what matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer work produced from an overpowering inner necessity to that which is merely argumentative, historical, or critical. Authentic, impassioned utterance is the key criterion: 'let me read his paper, and you may have all the arguments and histories and criticism.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols must be fluid, not fixed (anti-mysticism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the imagination is to flow, and not to freeze; mysticism mistakes an accidental and individual symbol for a universal one by nailing a symbol to one sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold symbols lightly and be ready to translate them into equivalents others use. Prefer universal signs (an 'algebra') to rigid local symbols; avoid making a personal metaphor into an immutable dogma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet must see nature 'beneath him' and use it as exponent
rubrics_metrics.description: All books of the imagination endure which ascend to that truth that the writer sees nature beneath him, and uses it as his exponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieve a standpoint where particulars serve as vehicles for the poet's larger insight—when a verse or sentence expresses that vision it secures its own immortality. The poet's task is to make objects exponents of new thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express symmetrically and abundantly (avoid fragmentariness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the path of the creator to his work; the painter, sculptor, composer, epic rhapsodist, orator—all partake one desire to express themselves symmetrically and abundantly, not dwarfishly and fragmentarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue a beauty half-seen which flies before you; persist until the dream-power pours out. Aim for breadth and abundance of expression—when the poet attains that power his genius is no longer exhaustible and can pour all creatures and impressions into his work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to renounce worldly life for the muse
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet must leave the world and know the muse only; he must abdicate a manifold life, be content that others speak for him, lie close hid with nature, and pass for a fool or churl for a long season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept apprenticeship and sacrifice as part of poetic vocation. The constraint and isolation protect the work ('the screen and sheath in which Pan has protected his well-beloved flower') and yield the reward that the ideal becomes real to the poet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and comprehensiveness: seek inexhaustible richness
rubrics_metrics.description: Rich poets (Homer, Chaucer, Shakespeare, Raphael) have obviously no limits to their works except the limits of their lifetime and resemble a mirror ready to render an image of every created thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate an imagination capacious enough to receive and transmute the full variety of nature and human life; the greatest poets can make virtually any object or scene available as material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate your times and social circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets should chaunt their own times and social circumstance rather than avoid them; contemporary life (banks, politics, Methodism, tariffs, races, local scenes) rests on the same foundations of wonder as Troy or Delphi and is worthy of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the national or local materials of your own age and treat them as poetic matter. A timely poet renders the contemporary world into universal art—America itself 'is a poem' worth metre and celebration.

rubrics_metrics.name: An imaginative work first stimulates more than it explains
rubrics_metrics.description: An imaginative book renders us much more service at first by stimulating us through its tropes than afterward when we arrive at the precise sense of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize works that stir and liberate the reader; the initial imaginative impact matters more than eventual precision of literal meaning. Stimulation of new sense is a primary value of poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept transience of moods; live and work in the present
rubrics_metrics.description: Life is a train of moods; perception and passion are transient, and the true art of life is to 'fill the hour'—to finish the moment and find the journey's end in every step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not postpone engagement with present duties and companions; treat the actual people and circumstances with justice and attention. Practical presence and completing each moment are marks of wisdom and sustain creative life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance thought with action; avoid mere intellectual criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual tasting of life will not supersede muscular activity; criticism and abstract thought alone cannot accomplish real results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground literary or philosophical work in active living; cultivate sturdy habits and the ability to 'fill the hour' with practical, well-mixed activity. Avoid letting critique become a substitute for labor and life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and change sustain sanity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanity of mind consists in circulation and variety of objects; we need change of objects and association to avoid stagnation and to keep creative faculties active.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate attention among books, people, and scenes; accept that enthusiasm for any single book or work will ebb. Use variety of stimuli to renew perception and prevent fixation that deadens response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperament limits but does not finally determine the creative act
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperament is the iron wire on which beads (moods) are strung and acts as a limiting force that shapes activity, yet there is a door in every intelligence through which the creator passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize temperament's constraints (some men are temperamentally fixed), but trust that the intellect or heart can intervene to break deterministic limits. Do not let physiological or pseudo-scientific accounts become an excuse to renounce creative striving.
